dimensions.summary: web app; no clear entry point; 1 import cycle(s).
9 source files; 1 over 500 lines; 26 TODOs; max complexity 29; 1 parse error(s).
5 dependency/hygiene finding(s); no lockfile; 2 unpinned dependency string(s).
Basic pattern checks only; 1 secret-like match(es); 1 dynamic-execution and 1 debug finding(s).

findings.title: Python parse error
findings.why: A file that does not parse cannot be analysed or imported safely.
findings.recommendation: Fix the syntax error and re-scan to restore full analysis coverage.

findings.title: Very large source file
findings.why: Very large modules are hard to review, test and change safely.
findings.recommendation: Map the relevant tests, then extract one cohesive concern at a time.

findings.title: Very high cyclomatic complexity
findings.why: Very high branching complexity makes a function hard to test exhaustively.
findings.recommendation: Split the function by responsibility and add regression tests for each branch.

findings.title: Secret-like string in a tracked file
findings.why: A credential committed to source should be treated as compromised.
findings.recommendation: Remove the value from history, rotate the credential and load it from the environment.

findings.title: Import cycle between 2 source modules
findings.why: Import cycles make startup order fragile and prevent clean layering.
findings.recommendation: Break the cycle by moving shared contracts into a lower-level module.

findings.title: Long function
findings.why: Long functions mix steps that can usually be named and tested separately.
findings.recommendation: Extract one named step at a time, preserving behaviour with tests.

findings.title: Dangerous dynamic execution pattern
findings.why: Dynamic execution is a common path for injection bugs.
findings.recommendation: Prefer explicit calls or strict allow-lists; document why dynamic execution is required.

findings.title: Hardcoded debug mode
findings.why: Debug mode enabled in tracked code can leak stack traces and internal state.
findings.recommendation: Drive debug settings from environment configuration and default to off.

findings.title: Manifest present but no lockfile
findings.why: A lockfile makes installs reproducible across machines and CI.
findings.recommendation: Generate and commit the lockfile for the package manager in use.

findings.title: Unpinned direct dependencies
findings.why: Loose dependency ranges make builds drift over time.
findings.recommendation: Pin direct dependencies to tested versions and let the lockfile handle transitives.

findings.title: No test files detected
findings.why: Without tests, changes to source behaviour cannot be verified automatically.
findings.recommendation: Add a small test suite around the main entry path and the riskiest modules.

findings.title: Application has no clear entry point
findings.why: Without an entry point it is harder to see how the application starts and where behaviour begins.
findings.recommendation: Add or document a single entry point (for example main.py, __main__.py or a console script).

findings.title: Test/source ratio below expected for this repository shape
findings.why: A low test/source ratio suggests large parts of the codebase have no direct tests.
findings.recommendation: Add focused tests for the highest-risk modules before broad refactoring.

findings.title: No README found
evidence: no README.md, README.rst or README.txt at the repository root
findings.why: A repository without a README gives a new developer no starting point.
findings.recommendation: Add a short README that states what the project is, how to run it and how to test it.

findings.title: No license file
evidence: no LICENSE, COPYING or NOTICE file found
findings.why: A repository without a license is not legally reusable by others.
findings.recommendation: Add the license you intend to use and reference it from the README.

findings.title: High TODO/FIXME density in source
findings.why: A dense backlog of inline TODOs signals unfinished or uncertain code.
findings.recommendation: Triage the markers: convert real work into issues and delete stale notes.

findings.title: No .gitignore
findings.why: Without ignore rules, local state and build output can be committed by accident.
findings.recommendation: Add a .gitignore for the toolchain in use.

findings.title: No CI configuration
evidence: no GitHub Actions, GitLab CI or equivalent configuration
findings.why: Automated checks catch regressions that a local scan cannot.
findings.recommendation: Add a minimal CI job that runs tests and quality checks.

actions.title: Remove and rotate hardcoded secrets
actions.why: Committed credentials must be treated as compromised before any other refactor.

actions.title: Reduce oversized source files in small, test-backed moves
actions.why: Large files dominate review cost and make changes riskier.

actions.title: Split high-complexity functions and add branch tests
actions.why: Complex branching is the most expensive code to change safely.

exclusions.reason: Documentation translations, examples, generated files and vendored code do not drive source quality.

limitations: Security checks are basic pattern checks only; they are not a security audit.
Documentation content is read only for README unless --include-docs is used.
Churn requires a git repository and recent history.
Non-Python languages use conservative heuristics, not deep semantic analysis.
Churn requires a git repository; hotspot churn rules were skipped.
The overall score is capped at A+: the analysed code is too small to demonstrate the sustained quality the top of the scale implies.
